articles.title: Why Your Testers Can't Opt In: Fixing Google Play's Opt-In Friction
articles.excerpt: You have 12 testers lined up. You send them the opt-in link. And then the messages start arriving: "the link doesn't work," "it says I'm not eligible," "I signed in but nothing happened." Every day a…
articles.body: You have 12 testers lined up. You send them the opt-in link. And then the messages start arriving: "the link doesn't work," "it says I'm not eligible," "I signed in but nothing happened." Every day a tester spends stuck on the opt-in screen is a day your 14-day clock is not counting properly — or worse, a day you lose a tester you already recruited. The opt-in step looks trivial. It is where more closed tests stall than anywhere else. Most opt-in failures come down to three things: the wrong link, the wrong account, or a tester who was never actually eligible. All three are fixable, and none of them require restarting your 14 days. The opt-in link is not the Play Store link This is the single most common mistake.

articles.title: How Much Are Claude Code, Codex & OpenCode Actually Costing You? (Zero-Dependency Local Spend Auditor)
articles.excerpt: If you bounce between Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Google Antigravity, OpenCode, xAI Grok CLI, and Cline / Roo Code, you quickly run into a blind spot: every agent stores local token telemetry in a…
articles.body: If you bounce between Claude Code , OpenAI Codex CLI , Google Antigravity , OpenCode , xAI Grok CLI , and Cline / Roo Code , you quickly run into a blind spot: every agent stores local token telemetry in a completely different format — and even uses incompatible prompt-cache accounting rules. Anthropic / Antigravity / OpenCode log uncached input, cache_read , and cache_write as separate additive buckets ( total_input = input + cache_read + cache_write ). OpenAI / Codex CLI / Grok CLI log cached_tokens as an inclusive subset already inside input_tokens (plus Codex silently compresses older sessions into ~/.codex/archived_sessions/*.jsonl.zst , while OpenCode v2 migrated from JSON files to a local SQLite opencode.db ).

articles.title: What Is a Face Embedding? How Facial Recognition Turns Faces Into Vectors
articles.excerpt: Not a photo, not a fingerprint image, a string of numbers that represents a face well enough to compare it to another. (Originally published on the FaceTrust AI Blog) A face embedding is a fixed-lengt…
articles.body: Not a photo, not a fingerprint image, a string of numbers that represents a face well enough to compare it to another. (Originally published on the FaceTrust AI Blog ) A numeric representation, not an image A face embedding is a fixed-length vector of numbers, often several hundred dimensions, produced by a neural network from a face image. It's not a compressed photo; it's a mathematical representation of the facial features the network was trained to distinguish. Why that representation is useful Two embeddings generated from photos of the same person end up numerically close to each other, while embeddings from different people end up further apart. Comparing two faces becomes a matter of measuring the distance between their embeddings.

articles.title: Getting 40% more token throughput from our local product-enrichment pipeline
articles.excerpt: At Yuh Gettin’ Tru, we use a local model to help turn retailer product data and images into descriptions for semantic search. I recently switched the model build running under oMLX on my MacBook M4 Pr…
articles.body: At Yuh Gettin’ Tru , we use a local model to help turn retailer product data and images into descriptions for semantic search. I recently switched the model build running under oMLX on my MacBook M4 Pro. Observed throughput went from 18.7 to 26.2 tokens per second , with near-identical results for our workload. That’s about a 40% improvement, using the same base model. The newer build is also smaller. This seemed worth writing up because the improvement came from revisiting the model and inference software we were already using, rather than changing the application architecture. What the pipeline actually does Yuh Gettin’ Tru helps people find products across retailers in Barbados. One of the challenges is that different stores describe the same kinds of products very differently.

articles.body: Voyager 1 is celebrating a big milestone as it approaches its 50th birthday: reaching one light-day away from Earth. NASA's long-running interstellar Voyager 1 probe will mark one light-day of distance from Earth on Nov. 18, when the spacecraft is 49 years, two months and 11 days old. The agency recently stated the record distance, which will be reached at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (101607 GMT) is "a huge milestone by any measure, and a day worth celebrating." During the light-day crossover, Voyager will be in contact with the Madrid station of the three-antenna Deep Space Network that monitors all deep-space missions.
